\paragraph{Model Fidelity and Compounding Error.}
\citet{chua2018pets} demonstrate that probabilistic ensembles can quantify dynamics-model uncertainty for planning, but this uncertainty is consumed by the planner rather than bootstrapped through a critic. \citet{lambert2020objective} formalize the \emph{objective mismatch} problem: minimizing observation-prediction loss does not guarantee reward-prediction accuracy. \citet{asadi2019combating} and \citet{lambert2022investigating} characterize compounding prediction error in multi-step model rollouts as a fundamental challenge for model-based methods. \citet{ma2024harmonydream} address this in DreamerV3 by harmonizing reconstruction and reward loss weighting. Our gradient decomposition (\S\ref{sec:gradient_decomposition}) provides direct evidence: at convergence, 93\% of temporal embedding gradients originate from observation decoders while the reward head's contribution diminishes to negligible levels, confirming that observation reconstruction dominates embedding learning. \citet{palenicek2025diminishing} show diminishing returns of value expansion with increasing rollout length, consistent with our finding that $\dt > 1$ imagination compounds model errors without proportional benefit. \citet{frauenknecht2025rollouts} demonstrate rollout-quality dominance in MBRL; we identify the specific $\dt$-embedding-induced mechanism by which rollout divergence corrupts values.

1	Temporal abstraction via variable-rate imagination is a natural extension of world-model reinforcement learning, yet we find that every variable-rate configuration of DreamerV3 degrades performance---despite the success of identical $\Delta t$-conditioning in MPC-based methods.
